decks.title: The Organizational Context: Strategy, Structure, and Culture

questions.p: Project management is the application of ______ to project activities to meet project requirements.
o: These come from governance, which guides projects. They are not what the definition says is applied.
These are things a project manager manages or produces. The definition names what is applied to the work, not the items being controlled.
These are the four nouns in the definition: what you know, what you can do, what you use and the methods you follow.
This sounds right, but it is a general management phrase and not the definition. Products are what a project creates, not what it applies.

questions.p: A PM spends the week removing blockers, aligning the team on priorities and checking that the work still leads to what the client needs. She writes no code. Which statement describes this?
o: She is doing project management, which means guiding the work to deliver the intended outcomes
The slide defines project management as guiding the project work toward the intended outcomes, so a PM can do it without producing deliverables herself.
She is doing product management, because she focuses on what the client needs
Product management runs across a product’s whole life cycle. Guiding one project’s work toward its outcomes is project management.
She is not doing project management, because she is not producing deliverables
Producing deliverables is the team’s work. The PM’s contribution is guiding that work.
She is doing general management, because she has no technical tasks
General management runs ongoing operations. The lack of technical tasks doesn’t change that this is temporary project work.

questions.p: A team must follow fixed regulations and has stable requirements, so it plans the entire project up front. Which approach is this?
o: Decentralized describes how a team is coordinated, not how the work is planned.
Hybrid mixes up-front planning with iterative work. Nothing here is iterative.
Predictive means detailed planning up front, which suits stable, well-understood requirements.
Adaptive works in short cycles and expects requirements to change, which is the opposite of this team’s situation.

questions.p: According to PMI, how many people will employers need in project management–oriented roles by 2027?
o: This is the total need by 2027, as stated on the slide.
This is the number of new PM employees needed each year to 2030, not the total for 2027.
This resembles the $135.2 billion Saudi AI market figure on the next slide.
This confuses the figure with the waste statistic on the next slide: $97 million per $1 billion spent.

questions.p: PMI’s Talent Gap report says 2.3 million new project management employees will be needed each year to meet global demand by 2030.
o: That is the slide’s figure: 2.3 million per year up to 2030, as distinct from the 87.7 million total roles by 2027.
The statement is correct. The two numbers measure different things: 87.7 million is the total by 2027, and 2.3 million is the new people needed each year to 2030.

questions.p: Which set lists the top skills employers look for in new graduates, according to the slide?
o: These are technical skills. The slide’s point is that employers’ top skills are not technical ones.
All three are skills that managing projects builds, which is the slide’s reason for mentioning them.
These appear in the competencies on slide 17, not in this list of graduate skills.
These are PM tasks, not the skills listed as top employer requirements for graduates.

questions.p: A company spends $2 billion on projects. Based on PMI’s Pulse of the Profession figure, about how much would it waste?
o: This multiplies by ten. It would mean almost half the money is wasted.
This assumes 1% waste, but the actual rate is close to 10%.
The rate is $97 million per $1 billion, so $2 billion gives 2 × $97M = $194M.
This is the waste for $1 billion. The company spends twice that.

questions.p: What does the slide say about Saudi Arabia’s government technology spending in 2025?
o: These figures describe the expected AI market and its share of GDP by 2030, not 2025 government spending.
The amount is right, but 12.4% is the AI market’s expected contribution to GDP.
This is PMI’s project waste figure, unrelated to Saudi spending.
About $24.7 billion, the highest in the world, 21.7% of national spending
All three details come from the slide.

questions.p: Which three things does the slide say help you understand the project management profession?
o: Its budgets, schedules, and quality standards
These are what a PM manages on a project, not the background to the profession.
The 12 principles, 8 domains, and the system for value delivery
These come from the PMBOK standard, covered later in the deck.
Its history, professional societies such as PMI, and the growth in project management software
These three are named together on the slide.
These are delivery approaches, not what the slide lists for understanding the profession.

questions.p: According to the slide, the project management profession is growing slowly as companies move away from formal management.
o: Check the wording: the slide says it is growing “at a very rapid pace”. The statement says the opposite.
The slide says the profession is growing at a very rapid pace.

questions.p: Which project is usually considered the first to use “modern” project management?
o: Some argue it was a project, but the slide does not call it modern project management.
Same as the pyramids: arguably a project, but not “modern” project management.
It isn’t on the slide. It came later than the Manhattan Project, which holds this title.
Most people consider it the first, partly because of its separate project and technical managers.

questions.p: What was distinctive about how the Manhattan Project was organized?
o: The technical manager also managed the budget and schedule
This merges the two roles, which is exactly what the project avoided.
It was run by a PMO
PMOs became common in the 1990s, decades later.
Teams self-organized with no designated managers
This describes decentralized coordination, covered on slide 39. The Manhattan Project had designated managers.
It had a separate project manager and technical manager
Separating managerial and technical leadership is the structural lesson the slide highlights.

questions.p: A $2 billion (1946 dollars), three-year effort: what do these numbers tell you about why modern project management emerged?
o: Projects only need managing when they cost over $1 billion
No such threshold exists, and small projects also benefit.
At that scale and with that deadline, informal coordination was no longer enough
Size, time pressure and many sites are the conditions that make formal management necessary.
Government projects must always have two managers
The two-manager split was this project’s choice, not a rule about government work.
Three years is the maximum length of a project
A project is temporary, but the definition sets no maximum length.

questions.p: Why did many companies begin creating PMOs in the 1990s?
o: To obtain PMP certification for the company
PMP is a certification for individuals, not a reason for creating a PMO.
To replace project managers with a central team
A PMO supports and coordinates PMs. It doesn’t replace them.
To take over the ongoing operations of the company
Operations are the organization’s routine work. A PMO’s focus is the project management function.
To handle the increasing number and complexity of projects
This is the reason the slide gives: too many complex projects to coordinate informally.

questions.p: A PMO is best described as:
o: A person assigned to lead a single project team
That is the project manager (slide 26). A PMO works across projects.
An organizational unit responsible for coordinating the project management function throughout an organization
This is the slide’s definition. Note “throughout an organization”.
A group of related projects managed for extra benefits
A software tool for scheduling tasks
A PMO is a unit of people, though it may choose and support such tools.

questions.p: A project finished on time and on budget, yet six months later almost nobody uses the system. Which global issue from the slide does this highlight?
o: Benefits realization of projects is a key metric
Success is now judged by whether the promised benefits actually arrive, not only by delivery.
The problem here is the lack of results, not a shortage of skilled managers.
This says basic PM skills are widely expected. It doesn’t explain unused deliverables.
The move to more agile approaches
Agile could help, but the issue described is measuring realized benefits.

questions.p: A company adds “can plan and track a small project” to every engineer’s job requirements. Which dynamic is this?
o: Basic project management techniques are core competencies
Core competency means an ability expected widely, not only from people titled PM.
Talent development for project and program managers
This concerns developing PMs specifically, whereas this requirement applies to all engineers.
This concerns measuring project results, not staff abilities.

questions.p: Struggling to find enough experienced program managers, a company launches a mentoring path for them. Which dynamic does this respond to?
o: Mentoring managers doesn’t make the delivery approach more agile.
This measures the results of projects, not the supply of managers.
Talent development for project and program managers
The slide calls this a top concern, and a mentoring path is a direct response.
This is about broad basic skills, not growing specialized managers.

questions.p: The slide says organizations want to use less agile approaches to project management.
o: Read carefully: the slide says “more agile”. Organizations want to respond faster to change, not more slowly.
The slide says organizations want to use more agile approaches.

questions.p: Which organization is described as the leader in advancing the project management profession?
o: PMI also publishes the PMBOK standard and runs the certifications.
IEEE is an engineering body, and it is not the one named on this slide.
A PMO is a unit inside a single organization, not a professional body.
This national strategy was mentioned on slide 6 as a source of demand.

questions.p: A third-year student with no project experience wants a PMI certification. Which one does the slide point to?
o: The slide says students can join PMI at a reduced fee and earn the CAPM.
A PMO is an organizational unit, not a certification.
PMBOK is the body of knowledge, not a certification.
The PMP suits experienced practitioners, so it isn’t the entry-level option for students.

questions.p: The number of people earning PMP certification is decreasing quickly.
o: The slide says it is increasing quickly, which fits the growing demand for PM skills.
The slide says the number is increasing quickly.

questions.p: Ethics is loosely defined as:
o: The principles that make a project finish on time
Ethics concerns right and wrong, not schedule performance.
A set of principles that guide decision making based on personal values of right and wrong
This is the slide’s definition. The words “personal values” are key.
The set of laws that governs a project
Laws are external and legal. Something can be legal yet unethical.
A list of tasks each team member must perform
That describes a work plan, not ethics.

questions.p: The sponsor asks the PM to report the project as “green” until the funding decision, although it is two months late. What is this?
o: Tailoring, because the report is adapted to the audience
Tailoring adapts methods to context. It doesn’t allow false information.
Hiding a delay does nothing to address the delay. It only deceives the people deciding on funding.
An ethical dilemma: pressure to misreport conflicts with honesty
PMs often face this kind of pressure, and the slide says so directly. Honesty is one of PMI’s four values.
Stakeholder engagement, because the sponsor is being kept happy
Engagement requires honest communication, not misleading a decision-maker.

questions.p: What must applicants agree to in order to earn the PMP certification?
o: This is a concept in the standard, not an agreement applicants sign.
Governance belongs to each organization, while PMP is a professional certification.
PMI’s Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
The slide states this requirement, and adds that the exam includes questions on professional responsibility.
These are studied for the exam, but applicants don’t sign an agreement to them.

questions.p: The PMP exam includes questions related to professional responsibility, including ethics.
o: The slide says several exam questions cover this, so ethics counts as part of being qualified.
The slide says “several questions” on the PMP exam relate to professional responsibility, including ethics.

questions.p: A client wants delivery a month earlier with the same features. What should the PM expect?
o: Only the schedule document needs to be updated
A new date on paper doesn’t change the amount of work that must be done.
Nothing else changes if the team works efficiently
Efficiency helps, but ignoring the trade-off is how projects end up over budget or full of bugs.
Quality improves because the team is more focused
Time pressure usually reduces quality rather than improving it.
Cost will likely rise or quality will likely suffer, because schedule, budget and quality are linked
These constraints trade against each other. Moving one affects the others.

questions.p: Another project is about to take the only security engineer next month. Which PM responsibility from the slide applies?
o: Securing people and equipment before others claim them is what this item means.
This concerns getting results to the customer, not securing staff.
Losing the engineer may affect quality, but securing that person is a resource responsibility.
Status tells you what has been done. It doesn’t secure the people you’ll need.

questions.p: What does the slide say consumes most of a project manager’s time?
o: Negotiation is a competency on slide 17, but not what the slide says takes the most time.
Chasing and collecting the status of project tasks
This is the slide’s closing point, and it is why tracking tools matter.
Writing code for the difficult parts
The team does that work. The PM guides it.
Budget is a PM responsibility, but the slide says status takes up most of the time.

questions.p: The issues a project manager handles stay the same regardless of the project’s scale.
o: The slide says issues vary with scale. A small internal tool and a national system bring different problems.
The slide says the issues “may vary depending on the project scale”.

questions.p: Which list matches the responsibilities most PM job descriptions include, according to the slide?
o: These belong closer to governance and compliance roles.
Planning, scheduling, coordinating, and working with people
This is the wording on the slide. All four concern getting people’s work organized.
Hiring, firing, promoting, and paying staff
These usually belong to functional managers or HR, not to the PM.
These are engineering tasks the team performs.

questions.p: What does the 97% statistic on the slide tell you?
o: 97% of successful projects were led by experienced project managers
The slide uses this to show that experience influences success.
97% of projects succeed when using PMBOK
The statistic concerns who led them, not which standard they used.
The number describes successful projects, not the whole PM population.
97% of a PM’s time goes to status collection
Status is mentioned on the previous slide, with no such percentage.

questions.p: A PM is talented technically, but keeps getting surprised that a department head can quietly block decisions. Which skill from the slide is missing?
o: The problem here isn’t change. It is not knowing how the organization makes decisions.
The department head isn’t on the team. The gap is about understanding the organization.
The PM already has these, and the situation shows they aren’t enough.
Understanding the organization they work in and with
Knowing how power and decisions really work in the organization is this skill.

questions.p: Halfway through, the client changes direction, and the PM calmly replans instead of resisting. Which skill is this?
o: This case is about reacting to a change, not about internal politics.
Nobody is in conflict in this scenario.
Plans will change. A PM who can adjust calmly keeps the project moving.
This secures people and equipment. It isn’t about responding to a new direction.

questions.p: A PM needs a database expert who reports to another manager, and must agree on how many days she can have him. Which competency does this use?
o: Mentoring develops someone’s abilities. It doesn’t secure their time.
Reaching an agreement over a shared resource with someone who doesn’t report to you is negotiation.
Listening helps, but the core activity here is bargaining for a resource.
She isn’t using technical knowledge to get the expert’s time.

questions.p: A PM keeps the same standards for everyone and always does what she says she will. Over time, the team tells her about problems early. Which competencies explain this?
o: Integrity, ethical and consistent behavior, and building trust
Consistency builds trust, and trust makes people bring bad news early.
Nothing here depends on technical ability.
Reasoning well doesn’t by itself make the team open up.
This concerns senior decision-makers, not how the team feels about her.

questions.p: A senior engineer spends an hour a week helping a new graduate learn how to estimate tasks. Which competency is this?
o: Developing another person’s abilities over time is mentoring.
This concerns decisions at the organizational level, not coaching one person.

questions.p: A key decision has been stuck with senior management for weeks. The PM builds support among other department heads to move it forward. Which competency is this?
o: Getting things moving above and across your position without authority is influence.
This is about forming your own team. The people here aren’t on it.
Listening alone won’t move a stalled decision.
Speaking is part of it, but the competency being used is influencing the organization.

questions.p: Three urgent requests arrive at the same time, and the PM decides which one matters most for the project goals. Which competency is this?
o: People skills help in relationships. This is a judgment about the work.
Deciding what matters most when several things compete is this competency.
No people are in dispute here. Only tasks are competing.

questions.p: Most of the 14 competencies for project managers are technical.
o: Count them: 13 of the 14 are about people, character or decisions, and only “process and technical” is technical.
Only one of the 14 (process and technical) is technical. The rest concern people, character and judgment.

questions.p: Which is NOT listed on the slide as an advantage of using formal project management?
o: No need for testing, since quality is planned in
Formal PM gives “higher quality and increased reliability”, but nothing suggests removing testing.
This is listed on the slide.
This is listed on the slide.
This is listed on the slide.

questions.p: After adopting formal PM, a team stops doing weekend crunches before each release. Which listed advantage does this show?
o: Fewer crunches may save money, but the scenario describes the effect on people.
The customer isn’t mentioned in this scenario.
Nothing here links the change to strategy.
Higher worker morale and less overworked personnel
Planned work spreads out the effort, reducing stress and overwork.

questions.p: The finance team can now see what each project spends and which staff it uses. Which listed advantage is this?
o: This concerns how staff feel, not financial tracking.
Better control of financial, physical, and human resources
Being able to see and steer money and staff is what control of resources means.
This concerns the product, not visibility into spending.
Visibility doesn’t by itself shorten delivery.

questions.p: Two departments stop duplicating work because their project plans are shared. Which listed advantage is this?
o: Different groups working from a shared plan is coordination.
This may follow, but the direct advantage described is coordination.
This is a distant effect. The scenario directly describes coordination.

questions.p: The Standard for Project Management applies only to large projects that use a predictive delivery approach.
o: The slide says “regardless of industry, location, size, or delivery approach”, so any statement limiting it to one kind of project is false.
It applies regardless of industry, location, size or delivery approach.

questions.p: What does the Standard for Project Management provide?
o: A fixed sequence of steps every project must follow
The standard guides understanding. It is not a required sequence.
PMP and CAPM are certifications. The standard is a reference.
A basis for understanding project management and how it enables intended outcomes
This is the slide’s statement of its purpose.
It discusses principles and systems, not specific templates.

questions.p: Besides the project itself, what does the standard describe?
o: Salaries and HR policies of the organization
These may be part of the environment, but they aren’t what the slide lists.
Only the project’s schedule and budget
Those are internal to a project, whereas the standard covers the surrounding system.
The standard isn’t tied to any technology.
Governance, possible functions, the project environment, and the relationship with product management
The slide lists these as the system within which projects operate.

questions.p: Which of the following best reflects the principle of “Stewardship” in project management?
o: Delegating all responsibility for ethical practices to external auditors
Stewardship is personal, so you can’t hand it off to auditors.
Taking personal responsibility for the careful use of resources, upholding values, and acting with integrity
Stewardship means acting with integrity, care, trustworthiness and compliance, inside and outside the organization. (Also Midterm 251 V2 MCQ 4.)
Focusing only on delivering project outputs, regardless of long-term impacts.
Stewardship looks beyond outputs to financial, social, technical and environmental impacts.
Ensuring accountability is limited to the project sponsor alone.
Everyone on a project is accountable for stewardship, not just the sponsor.

questions.p: A project team has limited resources and must choose the feature that will provide the greatest benefit to users. Which principle applies?
o: Value is the ultimate indicator of project success; prioritizing the most beneficial feature is focusing on value.
Navigating complexity deals with uncertainty and interacting factors. Here the decision is simply about which feature is worth most.
This is about responding to change and setbacks. Nothing has changed or gone wrong here.
Tailoring adapts the methods used. This decision is about what to build.

questions.p: Developers feel safe admitting mistakes in meetings, and they openly raise concerns. Which principle is being applied?
o: Leadership might foster this, but the scenario describes the team’s climate.
The slide describes Team as fostering trust, respect and open communication to empower members.
Stakeholders are usually outside the team. This scenario concerns how the team members treat one another.
Open communication may improve quality, but the behavior described is about the team.

questions.p: A PM brings end users into requirements sessions from the very first week. Which principle is this?
o: Nothing about the method is being adapted here.
Involving the people affected by the project is what this principle asks.
This principle supports the move to the new way of working. The scenario is early engagement.

questions.p: A small startup drops most of the heavy documentation its parent company requires, keeping only what is needed for a two-person project. Which principle is this?
o: Tailoring means adapting methods, tools and approaches to the situation.
Stewardship concerns responsible and ethical behavior, not adapting process.
Quality concerns building it in. Here the point is fitting the process to the project.
Complexity concerns uncertainty and interactions. Nothing here is complex.

questions.p: The team adds automated tests and code reviews from the first sprint instead of testing at the end. Which principle is this?
o: Value is about which outcomes are worth pursuing.
The focus here isn’t on trust or communication.
The slide says to ensure quality is embedded from the start.
Testing reduces risk, but “embedded from the start” is the slide’s wording for Quality.

questions.p: Before starting, the team lists what could go wrong and prepares a backup supplier. Which principle is this?
o: Identifying, assessing and responding to risks is this principle.
Complexity concerns uncertainty and interactions, while listing specific threats is risk work.
This is about reacting flexibly once things change. Here the team is preparing in advance.
This supports people through transformation, not planning for problems.

questions.p: When a vendor suddenly goes out of business, the team quickly switches to another and keeps going. Which principle is this?
o: Being flexible and ready to pivot when conditions change is this principle.
Tailoring adapts methods to the context. This is about recovering from a setback.
Nothing here is about ethics or care of resources.
Risk is about preparing beforehand. The scenario shows the response to an event that already happened.

questions.p: The PM helps staff learn the new system and move away from the old process over several months. Which principle is this?
o: The staff here are users of the new system rather than the project team.
Supporting transformation and continuous improvement is this principle.
Leadership helps, but the activity described is enabling the change.
Value concerns what is worth delivering. Here the focus is on people adopting it.

questions.p: A leader adjusts how she treats team members, patient with one who is struggling and direct with another who prefers it. Which principle is this?
o: Tailoring adapts project methods. Adapting personal style to people is leadership.
Team is about the shared climate of trust. Here the emphasis is on the leader’s behavior.
The slide says to lead with integrity, adaptability and empathy.
These are team members, and the focus isn’t on engaging outside parties.

questions.p: Nobody can predict how three new technologies and two departments will interact, so the team reviews the situation often and stays alert. Which principle is this?
o: The slide says to embrace uncertainty and complexity.
The team isn’t deciding what is most worthwhile.
Quality isn’t the subject of this scenario.
Risk works on specific identified threats. Here the unpredictability comes from many interacting factors.

questions.p: The PMBOK v7 principles are a sequence of steps to be carried out in order.
o: Principles guide how people behave. Nothing about them is a sequence, and the numbering is only a list.
They are guiding behaviors that apply throughout a project, with no required order.

questions.p: Which of the following best explains the nature of project performance domains?
o: They represent distinct areas of focus that guide effective project management.
Performance domains are areas of focus that run concurrently; they are not sequential processes or deliverables. (Also Midterm 251 V2 MCQ 1.)
They are rigid processes that must be followed in order, from initiation to closure.
Domains run at the same time and interact. They aren’t an ordered process.
They are optional tools that project managers may use only in large projects.
They apply to every project, whatever its size.
They are specific deliverables required at the end of each project phase.
Deliverables are what a project produces. Domains are areas you keep paying attention to.

questions.p: Which of these is NOT one of the 8 performance domains?
o: Procurement was a knowledge area in older PMBOK editions, and it is not one of the eight.

questions.p: How many project performance domains does PMBOK v7 define?
o: Five is the number of process groups in older PMBOK editions.
Ten was the number of knowledge areas in older editions.
That is the number of principles.
There are 8 domains and 12 principles. Don’t swap them.

questions.p: A team is deciding whether to work in sprints or plan everything first. Which domain does this fall under?
o: Planning organizes the work once the approach is chosen. The choice itself belongs to this domain.
Delivery concerns producing what’s required, not selecting the method.
Choosing how the work will be built and phased is this domain.
Uncertainty may influence the choice, but the decision belongs to the development approach.

questions.p: A PM tracks progress against targets and reports trends to the sponsor. Which domain is this?
o: The sponsor is a stakeholder, but the activity described is measuring performance.
Planning sets targets. Tracking against them is measurement.
This covers doing the daily work, not assessing how it is going.
Assessing performance and acting on it falls under Measurement.

questions.p: Performance domains are carried out one at a time: when the Planning domain ends, the Project Work domain begins.
o: That’s the classic trap. Domains aren’t phases, so planning continues while work is being done.
Domains run at the same time throughout the project and affect each other.

questions.p: “Projects, programs, subsidiary portfolios, and operations managed as a group to achieve strategic objectives” defines a:
o: A program groups related work for coordinated benefits, and doesn’t include operations in its definition.
A product is a quantifiable artifact, not a group of work.
This term isn’t defined on the slide, and it isn’t a grouping for strategic objectives.
It is the only grouping that includes operations and is defined by strategic objectives.

questions.p: A team ships a new online ordering system, and average customer wait time falls by 30%. Which is the outcome?
o: That is an output (the artifact). The outcome is what it changes.
A plan is a working document, not a result of the project.
The team produces the result. It isn’t the result.
An outcome is the result or consequence, focused on the benefit the project was undertaken to deliver.

questions.p: A company groups an R&D program, a marketing campaign and an infrastructure upgrade together for strategic oversight, though they are unrelated. What is this?
o: A program’s items must be related and coordinated for extra benefits. These are unrelated.
A project is a single temporary effort, not a group of different efforts.
A portfolio’s items can be unrelated. What unites them is the strategic objectives.
Operations are ongoing business functions. They can belong to a portfolio but aren’t the grouping itself.

questions.p: Which of these fits the definition of a product?
o: A meeting is an activity and produces no artifact in itself.
Strategy isn’t a quantifiable produced artifact.
This is an outcome rather than an artifact.
A payment module that is one component of a larger app
A product is produced and quantifiable, and it can be a component item.

questions.p: Outcomes can include outputs and artifacts, but they focus more broadly on the benefits and value the project was undertaken to deliver.
o: This is the slide’s wording: outcomes include outputs, with broader intent.
The statement is correct: outputs can be part of an outcome, but outcomes focus on benefits and value.

questions.p: A group of related projects managed in a coordinated manner to obtain benefits not available from managing them individually is called a:
o: A program is related projects managed together for benefits; a portfolio groups projects, programs and operations for strategic objectives and they can be unrelated. (Also Midterm 251 V2 MCQ 3, options shuffled.)
A portfolio can hold unrelated work and is defined by strategic objectives, not by coordinated benefits.
A project is a single temporary effort, not a coordinated group.
This term isn’t defined in this deck, and it doesn’t describe a group of coordinated projects.

questions.p: A company runs monthly payroll using the same process every time. Is this a project?
o: Yes, because it involves several people
The number of people doesn’t define a project.
Yes, because each month’s payroll has a start and an end
Each cycle ends, but the work repeats the same way indefinitely, so it isn’t unique.
No. It is ongoing and repeated, so it is an operation
A project must be temporary and create a unique result. Payroll is neither.
It is a program, because it repeats
A program is a coordinated group of related projects, not repeated routine work.

questions.p: A project lasting four years cannot be considered “temporary”.
o: This is a common trap: temporary concerns having a defined start and end, regardless of the length.
Temporary means it has a beginning and an end, not that it is short.

questions.p: Every project must be part of a program or portfolio.
o: The slide says projects “can stand alone”. Belonging to a program or portfolio is possible but not required.
Projects can stand alone or be part of a program or portfolio.

questions.p: A company’s digital transformation combines several related projects so that their results work together in ways no single project could achieve. This is best called a:
o: A product is an artifact, not a set of coordinated projects.
A portfolio doesn’t require its items to be related. Here the relatedness is the point.
The slide uses digital transformation as its example of a program.
This is a portfolio inside a portfolio, which doesn’t describe coordinated, related projects.

questions.p: Who assigns the project manager, according to the definition?
o: PMI certifies people. It doesn’t assign them to projects.
The customer sets the need but doesn’t generally appoint the PM.
The organization doing the work assigns the person who leads the team.
A team doesn’t elect its PM.

questions.p: A PM sets up a meeting between the design and backend teams to clear a blocker so that they can keep moving. Which function is this?
o: Allocating budget or people is a different function, usually the sponsor’s.
Helping the team do its work toward the outcomes is facilitating.
She isn’t giving technical advice. She’s connecting the people who have it.
Processes are the plans, tracking and controls. Here she is helping people work together.

questions.p: A PM updates the schedule, tracks progress and enforces the change process. Which function is this?
o: Facilitating is about supporting the people, not the mechanics of tracking.
Governance sets the authority and rules. The PM runs the process within them.
Managing the processes to deliver the intended outcomes
Planning, tracking and controlling make up process management.
The team performs the work and produces deliverables.

questions.p: In the context of the “system for value delivery,” which of the following is the most accurate statement?
o: Only portfolios and programs contribute to value delivery in an organization, while projects and products have no significant role.
All five components can contribute, including projects and products.

questions.p: A tester on a software project does no planning or tracking. Which group is she in?
o: The project team, but not the project management team
She performs the project’s work, but isn’t directly involved in managing it.
Both, since all members manage the project
Only those directly involved in management activities belong to the management team.
Management team members manage the work. She doesn’t.
Testing is project work, so she is part of the project team.

questions.p: The “project management team” is best defined as:
o: The senior executives overseeing the portfolio
These people provide governance and direction, but they aren’t this team.
Customers are stakeholders, not project team members.
The members of the project team who are directly involved in project management activities
This is the slide’s definition. It is a subset of the project team.
All individuals performing the work of the project

questions.p: Portfolios, programs, projects, products, and operations can all be part of an organization’s system for value delivery.
o: The slide lists all five as possible parts.
The slide says exactly this: all five can be part of the system.

questions.p: An organization measures a project’s “benefits less the cost of achieving those benefits”. Which type of value is this?
o: Business value is determined with financial metrics like this one.
Customers value the use of specific features, not the organization’s finances.
Societal value concerns contribution to communities or the environment.
The slide doesn’t define this type.

questions.p: A project saves $5M per year and cost $2M to deliver. Using the slide’s definition, what is the first-year business value?
o: This adds the cost, which should be subtracted.
This is the cost, not the value.
This counts the benefits but ignores the cost.
Benefits ($5M) less the cost of achieving them ($2M).

questions.p: Users praise a new app because it lets them pay bills with a single tap. What kind of value do they see?
o: Business value is measured by the organization using financial metrics.
Customer value: the ability to use a specific feature
Customers can define value as the ability to use specific features or functions.
This concerns benefits to communities, not one user’s convenience.
The slide doesn’t include this type.

questions.p: A free flood-warning system protects villages but makes no profit. What value does it provide?
o: It makes no profit, so it provides little financial benefit to the organization.
Contribution to groups of people, communities or the environment is societal value.
Those affected may not even be customers. The value is to the community as a whole.
No value, since it makes no profit
Value isn’t only financial. That is the point of this slide.

questions.p: All stakeholders perceive a project’s value in the same way.
o: The slide says the opposite: customers, organizations and society each judge value differently.
The slide says different stakeholders perceive value in different ways.

questions.p: Which element of the system identifies internal and external factors that influence projects?
o: These identify who supports the project.
The slide says it identifies the internal and external factors that influence projects and value delivery.
These show how portfolios, programs, projects and products relate.
Governance provides policies and monitoring. It doesn’t identify outside influences.

questions.p: Policies and performance monitoring that guide project work belong to which part of the system?
o: Functions are the roles supporting a project.
This explains how projects produce value, not the rules guiding them.
The slide names policies and performance monitoring as examples of governance.
The environment covers influencing factors, whereas governance actively sets the rules.

questions.p: Which part of the system describes how portfolios, programs, projects and products relate?
o: This part is about how projects produce value.
This part is about the roles that support projects.
This part is about the factors influencing projects.
This is what the slide says that part identifies.

questions.p: Which part of the system identifies the functions that support projects?
o: This concerns how the disciplines relate.
As the name says, it identifies the functions that support projects.
This concerns surrounding factors, not who does what.
Governance provides oversight. It doesn’t list project functions.

questions.p: Which part of the system describes how projects operate within a system to produce value for organizations and stakeholders?
o: This covers influences on projects, not how they produce value.
This is the slide’s description of that first element.
This covers how the disciplines relate.

questions.p: A hospital project replaces paper forms with tablets so nurses spend less time on administration. Which way of creating value does it show?
o: Creating positive social or environmental contributions
The main gain is staff efficiency, not a wider social benefit.
Improving efficiency, productivity, effectiveness, or responsiveness
The work stays the same, but it gets done faster and better.
Creating a new product for customers
The tablets serve internal staff, and no new customer product is created.
This protects existing value, whereas here the process gets better.

questions.p: A company launches a new mobile banking app for its customers. Which way of creating value is this?
o: Creating a new product, service, or result that meets customers’ needs
Something new now exists that meets customers’ needs.
Efficiency would improve existing work. Here the main thing is the new product.
The app doesn’t by itself transform the organization.
Sustaining keeps existing value going. This is a new offering.

questions.p: A charity builds a solar-powered water system for remote villages. Which way of creating value is this?
o: This is a new contribution, not protection of an old benefit.
Improving efficiency concerns how existing work gets done.
Creating positive social or environmental contributions
The value is to people and the environment.
The charity isn’t changing how it operates.

questions.p: A ministry’s project moves its whole operation from paper to digital so that it can work in a new way. Which way of creating value is this?
o: Creating a product for end users
The focus is the organization’s transition.
Enabling the changes needed for transition to a desired future state
The organization is moving to a future state, not just improving a task.
It may become more efficient, but the main goal described is transforming how it operates.
Sustaining keeps things as they are, whereas this project changes them.

questions.p: A company upgrades an aging billing system so that it can continue serving customers as it has for ten years. Which way of creating value is this?
o: This is a commercial upgrade with no wider social aim.
Sustaining benefits enabled by previous programs, projects, or operations
Nothing new is added. The upgrade protects existing value.
The goal is continuity rather than a new future state.

questions.p: Projects exist as stand-alone efforts, outside any larger system.
o: Don’t confuse this with slide 25: a project can stand alone from a program or portfolio, but it still sits inside a larger system.
The slide says projects exist within a larger system, such as a governmental agency, organization or contractual arrangement.

questions.p: Which of these is an example of operations, as the slide uses the term?
o: The slide lists payroll, supply chain, finance and budgeting, HR and customer service.
The strategic grouping of all work
That is a temporary effort with a unique result, so it is a project.
A group of related upgrade projects

questions.p: Portfolios, programs, and projects influence each other as well as operations.
o: The slide says so directly. Influence runs in every direction.
The statement is correct. It is taken directly from the slide.

questions.p: Value can only be created by the components working together, never individually.
o: The slide says “individually and collectively”. A single project can create value on its own.
The slide says components can be used individually and collectively.

questions.p: Why does it matter that the components are “aligned with the organization’s strategy”?
o: So that all components report to one manager
Alignment concerns direction, not reporting lines.
So that every project uses the same method
Tailoring means methods can differ. Alignment concerns purpose.
So that operations can be replaced by projects
Operations remain necessary. They aren’t replaced.
So that the system’s work supports where the organization has decided to go
Alignment is what turns separate pieces of work into one system with a purpose.

questions.p: Any of the projects or programs in the system could include products.
o: The slide says this, since projects and programs often exist to create products.
The slide states this directly: any of the projects or programs could include products.

questions.p: Customer service tells a project team that users keep failing at one step, and the team changes the design. What does this show?
o: Operations can directly support and influence projects
Customer service is an operational function, and here it influences a project.
The project is out of scope
Nothing here suggests the change exceeds what the project agreed to do.
The information came from operations, not the portfolio.
Customer service has become part of the project team
It supplied information but did not join the team.

questions.p: Which of these belongs to the external environment?
o: These are the organization’s own procedures.
A competitor launching a similar product
Competitors are outside the organization’s control.
The company sets this itself, so it is internal.

questions.p: Which of these belongs to the internal environment?
o: Laws come from outside the organization.

questions.p: Which statement correctly describes how these fit together?
o: The value delivery system sits within the internal environment, which sits within the external environment
This is the nesting the slide’s diagram shows.
The external environment sits within the internal environment

The system and the environments are separate and don’t affect each other
They are nested, and outer ones influence inner ones.
The internal environment sits within the value delivery system
The system is inside the internal environment, not the reverse.

questions.p: Which sequence matches the value delivery chain?
o: Deliverables produce outcomes, outcomes create benefits, and benefits create value.
Deliverables must come before outcomes, and benefits before value.
Benefits come after outcomes, which come after deliverables.
This is the reverse. Value is the end of the chain.

questions.p: According to the slide, what are benefits?
o: The slide says outcomes create benefits, “which are gains realized by the organization”.
Something of worth, importance or usefulness
Artifacts handed over to the customer
The end result or consequence of a project

questions.p: Why does the slide recommend focusing on outcomes, choices, and decisions?
o: It emphasizes the long-range performance of the project
Nothing suggests this, and outcomes usually need more involvement.
It may take longer in the short term, and nothing here is about speed.
It removes the need for deliverables
Deliverables are still needed, since they produce the outcomes.

questions.p: An online portal is launched. Customers begin to use it, and call-center costs fall by 25%. Which is the benefit?
o: The organization gains by paying less. That is a benefit.
The project team that built it
A team produces the deliverable, so it isn’t a benefit.
This is the outcome that creates the benefit.

questions.p: Value is defined on the slide as something of worth, importance, or usefulness.
o: This is the slide’s definition, matching slide 28.
The statement is correct: those are the slide’s exact words for value.

questions.p: What do portfolios share with programs and projects?
o: The desired outcomes, benefits, and value
This is on the slide. Portfolios translate strategy into what the work must achieve.
That flows up from programs and projects to portfolios.
That is what senior leadership shares with portfolios.
That passes from programs and projects to operations.

questions.p: What does senior leadership share with portfolios?
o: The flow starts here, at the top.
This goes from programs and projects to operations.
These come from operations, going up.

questions.p: A project hands its system to the IT operations team. What should go with it?
o: Nothing, because operations must work it out for themselves
Without the information, operations can’t support what they receive.
These flow from leadership to portfolios, not with the deliverables.
These go up to senior leadership.
Information on support and maintenance for the deliverables
The slide says deliverables pass to operations along with this information.

questions.p: When does a value delivery system work most effectively?
o: When components work independently to avoid interference
Independence breaks the alignment the system depends on.
When only senior leadership receives information
Information has to flow among all components.
When information and feedback are shared consistently among all components
This keeps the system aligned with strategy and in harmony with the environment.
When information is shared only at the end of each project
Feedback has to be consistent, not only at the end.

questions.p: Information flowing from operations back to programs and projects mainly suggests:
o: Adjustments, fixes, and updates to deliverables
Operations use what was delivered, so they spot what needs fixing.
These go from portfolios to senior leadership.
Strategic direction comes from senior leadership.
Operations don’t set the project’s budget.

questions.p: What do programs and projects provide to portfolios?
o: Operations provide these to programs and projects.
This flows downward from senior leadership.
Performance information and progress on the desired outcomes, benefits, and value
This is how portfolios know whether the work is achieving what they asked for.
Portfolios provide these to senior leadership.

questions.p: What do portfolios provide to senior leadership?
o: This goes to operations with deliverables.
This flows downward, from portfolios to programs and projects.
This is the top step of the upward flow.

questions.p: What additional information do operations provide, according to the slide?

Operations see the real results, so they show whether the strategy is working.
Hiring decisions aren’t part of this information flow.
The list of principles to follow
How to write the project charter

questions.p: What does the governance system work alongside?

Governance helps evaluate external factors, but it works alongside the delivery system.
It runs beside the value delivery system, enabling smooth workflows, managing issues and supporting decisions.
Governance belongs to the organization, not the customer.

questions.p: Which of these is NOT listed as an element of a governance framework?

o: This concerns team self-organization, not an organizational review board.
The board is doing the project’s work
The board evaluates and decides. The project team still does the work.
Governance gives an integrated structure for evaluating changes, issues and risks
One structure handles them, whatever their source.
The project has lost its scope
Having a review doesn’t mean scope has been lost.

questions.p: Governance systems provide a framework with functions and processes that guide activities.

The slide says it includes defining authority to approve changes and make related decisions.

The environment covers influencing factors, not assigned authority.

questions.p: At which level does governance look at “benefits”?

The slide doesn’t pair operations with benefits.

Portfolios are one option, not a requirement.
Programs are one option, not a requirement.
A PMO exists only in some organizations.

Transferred to external auditors for oversight.
Auditors check compliance. They don’t make the project’s decisions.

This would be even more centralized, the opposite of what decentralized means.

questions.p: Each project function must be performed by exactly one dedicated person.

Functions can be fulfilled by one person, a group, or combined into defined roles.

questions.p: What actually drives project delivery, according to the slide?
o: Governance guides and decides. It doesn’t deliver.
People, by executing the functions the project needs
The slide’s first point is “People drive project delivery”.
Tools help, but it is people who use them to deliver.
A plan guides, but only people carry it out.

Only one type works for all projects
The slide says there are different types for different contexts.

Hybrid describes a delivery approach, not a coordination style.
Decentralized teams self-organize, with no single person assigning tasks.

This is the slide’s first point.
The sponsor provides resources and direction rather than delivering.

Governance guides and decides, but doesn’t deliver.

The needs of the project, organization and environment influence which functions are used
The slide says functions depend on deliverables, industry, organization and other variables.
The game project has no governance
Having no clinical reviewer says nothing about its governance.
One of the projects is doing it wrong
Both can be right, since each suits its own context.

The statement is correct: the slide lists deliverables, industry, organization and other variables as what decides this.

Allocating budget, personnel and infrastructure is this function’s example on the slide.
This defines success and progress, not resources.

This monitors progress. It doesn’t identify customer needs.
Facilitating helps the team work. It doesn’t bring market information.

o: Governance enforces standards rather than watching day-to-day progress.
Monitoring progress and performance is this function’s example.
This sets where the team should go. She’s checking progress.

o: The client isn’t helping the team’s process.
The client isn’t offering technical advice.
Where we’re going and how far we’ve come are exactly what this function provides.
This concerns market trends. Here the client is defining success and reviewing progress.

questions.p: A Scrum master runs stand-ups and workshops and removes obstacles. Which function is this?

Hosting meetings, workshops and stand-ups is this function’s example.

questions.p: A developer finishes the features assigned to her in this sprint. Which function is this?
o: Completing assigned deliverables is this function’s example.
Expertise means advising. She’s doing the work itself.
She isn’t supporting others’ work here.

questions.p: A cloud architect spends two hours advising the team on a data-storage decision, then returns to her own department. Which function is this?
o: She isn’t monitoring the project’s progress.
Advising on technical or domain-specific matters is this function.
She isn’t completing deliverables, only advising.
Her advice is technical, not about the market.

questions.p: A quality board checks that a project meets national regulations and internal standards. Which function is this?
o: The board isn’t allocating budget or people.
Enforcing regulatory and internal standards is this function.
This concerns goals and progress, not compliance.

questions.p: Environmental influences on a project can be:
o: Only neutral, as they stay outside the project
They can influence planning and other project activities.
A skilled team or a growing market would be favorable.
The slide lists all three, so a factor isn’t automatically a problem.
Environments are both internal and external.

questions.p: A strong local talent pool makes hiring easier for a project. How would you classify this influence?

It helps the project, so it’s a favorable influence.

questions.p: Internal and external environments can influence planning and other project activities.
o: This is the slide’s second point.
The statement is correct: the slide says these environments influence planning and other activities.

questions.p: Half of the developers have never used the cloud platform the project depends on. What kind of factor is this?
o: The market isn’t the issue. The skills gap is within the organization.
Staff skills belong to the organization, so this is internal.
This is about skills, not governing documents.
Research is an outside source of knowledge, unrelated to staff skills.

questions.p: A team reuses templates and lessons learned from a previous project. These are examples of:

Knowledge includes lessons learned and completed artifacts from previous projects.

o: Internal: resource availability, arising from another project
The slide says internal factors can come from another project.
This happened inside the company, not in the market.
Not an environmental factor at all
It clearly influences the project, so it is one.
External: because it’s outside your project
External means outside the organization, not outside your project.

questions.p: Which of these is NOT an internal environment factor?

A law comes from outside the organization.
Listed as internal on the slide.
Listed as internal on the slide.

A law comes from outside the organization.

questions.p: A competitor’s price drop forces a company to rethink its project’s business case. Which external factor is this?

No law or regulator is involved.
This means physical conditions such as location or weather.
A price drop isn’t a social or cultural matter.

Safety rules may be internal, but the heat itself is external.

questions.p: A team buys access to a commercial database of market data. How is this classified?
o: Data assets are the organization’s own data.

Cultural expectations are outside the organization’s control.

questions.p: According to the slide, the disciplines of portfolio, program, project, and product management are:

Products exist only during their projects
